×36

Gated DeltaNet

16 Q/K heads and 32 V/Z heads; a decaying matrix state processes the sequence.

Q/K/V

Projection → convolution → SiLU[B,T,8192]
↓
Q/K normalization + repeat; VEach [B,T,32,128]

Z gate

Project Z; bypass convolution[B,T,32,128]
↓
SiLU gate × normalized output[B,T,32,128]

Decay / update

in_proj_ba[B,T,64]
↓
b,a each 32 → beta,gEach [B,T,32]
Input projection and splitQ/K each [B,T,16,128]; V/Z each [B,T,32,128]
↓
Q/K/V depthwise causal Conv1d + SiLU[B,T,8192]kernel=4, groups=8192; Z bypasses convolution.
↓
Q/K L2 normalization; repeat heads twiceQ/K/V each [B,T,32,128]
↓
Gated Delta Rule[B,T,32,128]beta=sigmoid(b)；g=−exp(A_log)·softplus(a+dt_bias)。
↓
RMSNorm(output) ⊙ SiLU(Z)[B,T,32,128]
↓
Flatten + out_proj[B,T,2048]
  • in_proj_qkvz uses interleaved K-head groups: 128Q+128K+256V+256Z per group, totaling 16×768; it is not split into four equal parts.
  • Per-layer recurrent state [B,32,128,128]; convolution cache [B,8192,4]. These states are excluded from parameter counts.
  • This branch uses no RoPE and does not form an explicit T×S softmax matrix.

Gated full attention

16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim=256; output uses an elementwise sigmoid gate.

q_proj → Q + gateQ/gate each [B,T,16,256]
↓
k_proj / v_projK/V each [B,T,2,256]
↓
Q/K head-wise RMSNorm → partial RoPE64 rotary dimensions per head; 192 unchanged
↓
Causal GQA；KV repeat 8[B,16,T,S] → [B,T,4096]
↓
attention output ⊙ sigmoid(gate) → o_proj[B,T,2048]
  • partial_rotary_factor=0.25 → rotary_dim=64；RoPE theta=10000000。
  • Per-layer K/V caches each [B,2,S,256]; non-parameter state.

×48

Sparse MoE + shared expert

Each layer selects 10 of 512 experts; the shared expert is added after its own sigmoid gate.

Router Linear → softmax → Top-10 → renormalize[B·T,512] → [B·T,10]
↓
10 selected SwiGLU expertsEach expert: 2048 → 512 → 2048
↓
Weighted sum using routing weights[B·T,2048]
↓
Shared SwiGLU × sigmoid(shared_expert_gate(x))[B·T,2048]
↓
Add both paths → outer residual[B,T,2048]
  • Each expert: down(SiLU(gate(x)) ⊙ up(x)). No separate norm inside experts.
  • The config's intermediate_size=5120 is not instantiated in these MoE layers; moe_intermediate_size and shared_expert_intermediate_size are both 512.
  • All experts occupy storage; Top-10 only determines the current token's computation path.

Multi-token prediction auxiliary module

The released weights include one additional full-attention + MoE decoder; standard 48-layer backbone inference does not pass through it.

Separate RMSNorm on next-token embedding and upstream hidden stateEach [B,T,2048]
↓
Concat → fc[B,T,4096] → [B,T,2048]
↓
Independent Gated Attention + residual[B,T,2048]Same structure as the 12 full-attention backbone layers.
↓
Independent MoE + residual[B,T,2048]10 of 512 routed + 1 shared expert; expert weights are not shared with the backbone.
↓
MTP final RMSNorm → shared LM head[B,T,151936]
  • Exactly 1,650,471,424 additional parameters; fc has shape 2048×4096.
  • MTP uses the backbone token embedding and LM head; the header contains no second set of these matrices.
  • The backbone class in Transformers v4.57.1 does not execute MTP. It is listed separately as an auxiliary branch, not a standard 49th backbone block.

  • 79.674B denotes the standard causal LM backbone; 81.325B denotes the full released checkpoint including MTP. 80B is the rounded size in the model name.
  • All Linear and Conv1d layers are bias-free; dt_bias is a separate Gated DeltaNet time-step parameter, not a Linear bias.
  • B=batch size, T=current length, S=attention length including history. Weight matrices use [out,in]; branch weights are counted once.
  • Approx. 3B active parameters is neither the checkpoint total nor memory usage or FLOPs. Counting full input/output matrices and replacing 512 experts per layer with the selected 10 gives 3,874,929,408; embedding lookup actually accesses only selected rows.
